cards.text: The Israelites are camped in the Wilderness of Paran. Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader. He's talking about Canaan, the land He says He is giving to the Israelites.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses to send into the land of Canaan?

answers.text: Men to spy out the land
An army to take the land

cards.question: From each tribe, the LORD wants Moses to send one man who is a ___ among them.

cards.text: So at the LORD's command, Moses sends them out from the Wilderness of Paran, all of them leaders of Israel. Then comes the roster, twelve names, one for each tribe, and one worth remembering is Caleb son of Jephunneh, from the tribe of Judah.

cards.question: One of the spies is Hoshea son of Nun, from the tribe of Ephraim. Moses gives him a new name. What is it?

cards.text: Before they leave, Moses gives them the mission. Go up through the Negev and into the hill country, and see what the land is like.

cards.question: What does Moses want the spies to find out about the people living in Canaan?

answers.text: How strong they are and how many
What language they speak at home
Which gods they bow down to

cards.question: Moses tells the spies to skip checking out the land and just check out the people.

cards.text: Strong or weak? Few or many? Good or bad? Trees or no trees? Friend, Moses didn't send spies, he sent a SURVEY. Then he tells them, "Be courageous" and adds one last request.

cards.question: Moses asks the spies to bring back some ___ from the land.

cards.text: Good timing, too. It's the season for the first ripe grapes, and the spies go up and spy out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.
Through the Negev they come to Hebron, a city built seven years before Zoan in Egypt. Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai live there.

cards.question: Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, who live in Hebron, come from a family line. Whose descendants are they?

cards.text: Then, in a valley, they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes. One cluster, friend. Hold that thought.

cards.question: That single cluster of grapes takes some real effort to move. How do the spies carry it?

answers.text: On a pole between two men
In a basket on one man's back
Tied to the side of a donkey

cards.text: On a pole. Between TWO grown men. For ONE cluster! I carry a single chocolate chip across my bakery with my mustache and I need to sit down. And because of that cluster, the place is called the Valley of Eshcol.

cards.question: Grapes are the only fruit the spies take from the land.

cards.text: After forty days the spies come back to Moses, his brother Aaron and the whole congregation at Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Paran. They bring a report and show everyone the fruit.

cards.question: The spies start their report with the land itself. What do they tell Moses it's like?

cards.text: Then one word turns the whole report around: "Nevertheless". I heard that word a lot in my drawer days. Nice stamper. Nevertheless.

cards.question: After the good news about the land, what do the spies say about its people and its cities?

answers.text: The people are strong and the cities fortified
The people are few and the cities small
The people are friendly and the cities open

cards.question: The spies say they even saw the descendants of Anak in the land.

cards.text: Then they run down who lives where: Amalekites in the Negev, Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites in the hill country, and Canaanites by the sea and along the Jordan. Forty days, and these guys know every neighborhood.
Now the people need quieting down. One spy steps up and does it, right in front of Moses.

cards.question: Which spy quiets the people in front of Moses?
Caleb says Israel must go up and take possession of the land. Why does he say so?

answers.text: Because they can certainly conquer it
Because the people there will run away
Because the land is already empty

cards.text: Caleb is ready to GO. But the other men who went up with him? You know that group project where one person says we got this, and everybody else says do we though? That's this.

cards.question: The other spies say Israel cannot go up, because the people in the land are ___ than Israel.
The spies spread a bad report among the Israelites, and in it they say the land devours its inhabitants.

cards.text: Hold on. A minute ago it was milk and honey, and now the land EATS people? Same land. Same trip. Brand new review.
They say all the people they saw there are great in stature, and they even saw the Nephilim. They say the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim.

cards.question: Next to people that big, the spies feel tiny. What do they say they seemed like in their own sight?

cards.text: And they figure they must have seemed the same to them. I spent years seeing myself as a worn-out stamper in the back of a drawer, so I know that feeling. We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card says the Israelites are camped in the Wilderness of Paran. That detail comes from Numbers 13:3, but the card cites only Numbers 13:1-2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 4 sums up the roster (Numbers 13:3-15) as a long stretch. Card 5 then asks a choice question about Hoshea's renaming in 13:16, which is the closing line of that same name list.
findings.question: Is Numbers 13:16 ("These were the names... Moses gave to Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua") part of the long stretch, which would allow it only as a standout detail with no choice card? Or is it a separate moment that can get its own choice card?

findings.problem: Card 6 already says Moses tells the spies to "see what the land is like." That gives away the answer to this true/false statement about skipping the land. The card also asks about 13:19-20 before any story card has told those verses. They are told afterward on card 9.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has six sentences: four questions, the SURVEY line and the "Be courageous" line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has five sentences and more than two beats: the reaction to the pole, the chocolate chip joke and the naming of the Valley of Eshcol.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "His brother Aaron" is a fact from outside the passage, and it is stated with no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory detail: hearing "Nice stamper. Nevertheless" a lot during his drawer days. Nothing in the backstory has anyone speaking to him in the drawer. The image also needs explaining for a stranger to get it. The card also has four sentences.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Card 3 says "Nevertheless" turns the whole report around after the good news. That signals the next part is negative and rules out both wrong answers, which are positive: few people and small cities, friendly people and open cities.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The comparison uses a group project, which is a school scenario. The card also has three sentences.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids.

findings.problem: The true statement says "The spies" spread the bad report. Numbers 13:31-32 gives it to the men who went up with Caleb, not to Caleb, who argued the other way in 13:30. The statement also says "spread among," but the text says "gave the Israelites."

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card tells no new piece of the passage. It only replays milk and honey (13:27) next to the answer to card 12 (13:32). It also has five sentences.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question says "the spies feel tiny" and asks what "the spies" say they seemed like. In 13:31-33 the grasshopper words come from the men who went up with Caleb, not from Caleb.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the verse, the drawer reflection and the line saying the story isn't over.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the 8 choice cards in this stop. There are 2 true/false cards and only 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
